DECISION. Split into 11 children: 5 new nodes, plus 6 comparator-accepted declarations reused with byte-identical frozen types.

WHY SPLIT.
- When the handoff was written, the C¹-chart cover and the C¹-chart tangent identification existed only as speculative lpf nodes, so the supplied proof re-derived them inline. The lipschitz-pushforward branch has since accepted them, together with the chart tools that steps 3–8 use:
  - lpf_countably_rectifiable_c1_cover (step 3);
  - lpf_weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart (step 6);
  - lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables (step 5, for g ≥ 0);
  - lpf_ccr_ae_pullback (step 3(iv), used in steps 7–8);
  - lpf_wtc_cat_fderiv_lower_bound (step 3(ii));
  - lpf_tde_continuous_left_inverse (the left inverse (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ of step 8).
- The supplied proof explicitly allows reusing accepted lpf lemmas with identical types. The frozen proof base d38f8d26 is the bare contract, so these declarations can only be used as reused children. Otherwise the C¹ cover, the tangent-plane theorem and the area formula would all have to be re-proved inside this node.
- The remaining new work falls into five self-contained, reusable obligations of different kinds:
  - abstract measure theory (step 4);
  - the Bochner area formula on a chart (step 5);
  - measurable linear algebra (step 8);
  - Rademacher plus directional derivatives (steps 7(d) and 9(b));
  - chain-rule bookkeeping (step 9).

- continuous_left_inverse = lpf_tde_continuous_left_inverse (reused). The continuous left inverse in step 8.
- fderiv_lower_bound = lpf_wtc_cat_fderiv_lower_bound (reused). Step 3(ii): κ|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s| on Ω.
- partition_tendsto (new; no dependencies). Step 4: countable additivity over disjoint measurable pieces plus Tannery, for an abstract measure.
- chart_integral_eq (new; depends on chart_change_of_variables). Step 5, signed and Banach-valued: ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_{Ω∩Φ⁻¹(A)} JΦ·(F∘Φ).

ASSEMBLY OF THE PARENT (steps 1, 3, 4, 6 and 10 of the supplied proof; checked in Lean).
1. IsRectifiableTriple supplies:
   - M ⊆ U and M Hⁿ-null-measurable;
   - CountablyRectifiable n M;
   - θ > 0 on M, and θ integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U.
   countably_rectifiable_c1_cover then gives Φ_j and Ω_j (open, Φ_j C¹, K_j-Lipschitz and κ_j-antilipschitz on Ω_j) with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0.

Let V_j := disjointed (j ↦ Φ_j(Ω_j)). The V_j are Borel and pairwise disjoint, ⋃_j V_j = ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j), and V_j ⊆ Φ_j(Ω_j). For ν := Hⁿ⌞M, ν((⋃_j V_j)ᶜ) = Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0.

5. Fix j and let A := V_j ∩ M. Then A ⊆ Φ_j(Ω_j), A is Hⁿ-null-measurable, and Y is integrable on A. weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart with V := U and M, θ, Φ_j, Ω_j says: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j) and every w ∈ Ω_j with Φ_j(w) = x, range DΦ_j(w) is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M, θ) at x. Taking Q := range DΦ_j(w) gives the a.e. hypothesis of chart_representation: Y(x) ∈ range DΦ_j(w), plus the derivative clause of TG.
6. chart_representation gives c_j, integrable on Ω_j, with
   - ∫_A F_k dHⁿ = ∫_{Ω_j} D(g_k∘Φ_j)(c_j) (taking f := g_k, K := L);
   - ∫_A F_∞ dHⁿ = ∫_{Ω_j} D(h∘Φ_j)(c_j).
7. (Step 10.) Apply gradient_weak_star, the parent's own declared dependency, with Ω := Ω_j, C := L·K_j, u := h∘Φ_j, u_k := g_k∘Φ_j and c := c_j. By step 6 this is exactly the per-piece convergence that step 4 needs.
Step 2 of the supplied proof (the degenerate cases n = 0 and n > P) is no longer needed: every child, including both reused chart theorems, is stated and accepted for all P and n.

subproblems.title: C¹ chart cover of countably n-rectifiable sets (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2)
subproblems.statement: If M ⊆ ℝ^P is countably n-rectifiable, there are C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and open sets Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) such that each Φ_j is Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω_j and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)), CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (Φ : ℕ → Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : ℕ → Set (Eucl n)), (∀ j, IsOpen (Ω j)) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (Φ j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K (Φ j) (Ω j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω j, ∀ w' ∈ Ω j, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ j w - Φ j w'‖) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ ⋃ j, Φ j '' Ω j) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, “only if” part (printed proof adapted), used in Step 1 of the parent proof (Remark 1.3). Let M be countably n-rectifiable: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz (Definition 1.1).

1. Fix j. Apply the sibling lemma lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces to u := F_j and Ω := ℝⁿ (open; F_j is Lipschitz, hence locally Lipschitz): we get C¹ maps G_{j,k} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, open O_{j,k} with G_{j,k} antilipschitz on O_{j,k}, and Borel E_{j,k} ⊆ O_{j,k} with F_j = G_{j,k} on E_{j,k}, such that Lⁿ-a.e. w at which F_j is differentiable with injective derivative lies in ⋃_k E_{j,k}.

2. Decompose ℝⁿ = N_j ∪ C_j ∪ R_j, where N_j := {w : F_j not differentiable at w}, C_j := {w : F_j differentiable at w, DF_j(w) not injective}, R_j := {w : F_j differentiable at w, DF_j(w) injective}. These sets are Borel (the differentiability set is Borel and w ↦ fderiv F_j w is Borel measurable, Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). By Rademacher's theorem Lⁿ(N_j) = 0, and by step 1 Lⁿ(R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k}) = 0.

3. Hⁿ(F_j(N_j ∪ (R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k}))) = 0: F_j is Lipschitz with constant Λ_j, so Hⁿ(F_j(Z)) ≤ Λ_jⁿ Hⁿ(Z) = Λ_jⁿ Lⁿ(Z) = 0 for every Lⁿ-null Z ⊆ ℝⁿ (on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] = Lⁿ).

4. Hⁿ(F_j(C_j)) = 0, by the area formula (Simon: “by the area formula Lⁿ{x : JG_ij = 0} …”). In Lean this is directly SimonGMT `area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero` (Chapter02/AreaLipschitz.lean: critical and non-differentiability images of a Lipschitz map are Hⁿ-null). Mathematically: for the Lipschitz map F_j on the Borel set C_j, Simon Ch. 2 (3.4) (SimonGMT `area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity`) gives ∫_{ℝ^P} #(C_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{C_j} JF_j dLⁿ, where JF_j(w) = √det(DF_j(w)* DF_j(w)) (Jacobian of the within derivative, which agrees a.e. on C_j with DF_j). For w ∈ C_j, DF_j(w)*DF_j(w) is singular, so JF_j = 0 a.e. on C_j and the right side is 0. F_j(C_j) is Hⁿ-null-measurable (C_j is a countable union of bounded Borel sets of finite measure and F_j is Lipschitz; SimonGMT `nullMeasurableSet_image_of_lipschitzOn`), and the multiplicity is ≥ 1 on F_j(C_j), so Hⁿ(F_j(C_j)) = ∫ 1_{F_j(C_j)} dHⁿ ≤ ∫ #(C_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = 0.

5. For w ∈ E_{j,k}, F_j(w) = G_{j,k}(w) ∈ G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}). Hence F_j(ℝⁿ) ⊆ F_j(N_j ∪ (R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k})) ∪ F_j(C_j) ∪ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).

6. (Lipschitz bound by shrinking.) Each open O_{j,k} is the union of the countably many open balls B with rational centre and rational radius and closure B ⊆ O_{j,k}. On such B, ‖DG_{j,k}‖ is bounded on the compact convex set closure B, so by the mean value inequality G_{j,k} is Lipschitz on B (constant sup_{closure B}‖DG_{j,k}‖); and G_{j,k} is antilipschitz on B ⊆ O_{j,k} with the constant of O_{j,k}. Enumerate all triples (j, k, B) as l = 0, 1, 2, … (pad with Ω_l := ∅ if needed) and set Φ_l := G_{j,k}, Ω_l := B. Then each Ω_l is open, Φ_l is C¹ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`), Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω_l, and ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l) = ⋃_{j,k} G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).

7. By steps 3–6, M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j [F_j(N_j ∪ (R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k})) ∪ F_j(C_j)], a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Hence Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l)) = 0. ∎ (When n > P every set in ℝ^P is Hⁿ-null and the statement is immediate; the proof above also covers it.)
proof_key_steps: Write M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with F_j Lipschitz and apply lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces to each F_j on ℝⁿ.
Images of the non-differentiability set and of the uncovered regular set are Hⁿ-null (Rademacher, Lipschitz image bound).
The image of the critical set is Hⁿ-null by the area formula (Jacobian 0 there).
On E_{j,k}, F_j = G_{j,k}, so F_j(ℝⁿ) is covered up to null sets by the antilipschitz C¹ pieces G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).
Shrink each O_{j,k} to rational balls with compact closure inside to make the charts Lipschitz too; enumerate.

A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This lemma combines item (P4)(a),(b) of the parent proof with Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4/1.7, the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” and Remark 1.8(1) (printed arguments, specialized to one C¹ chart), as used in Steps 1, 5.3 and 7 of the parent proof. Setting: V ⊆ ℝ^Q open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V; Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q of class C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0). Put N := Φ(Ω). Recall η_{y,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − y) (`blowUpMap y λ`) and that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P means: dim P = n and for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_P φ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0. If n > Q then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^Q (Hausdorff dimension of ℝ^Q is Q; `hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt`) and there is nothing to prove; assume n ≤ Q.

0. (Preliminaries on the chart.)
 (a) For w ∈ Ω and s ∈ ℝⁿ: w + ts ∈ Ω for small t, and |Φ(w+ts) − Φ(w)| ≥ c|t||s|; dividing by |t| and letting t → 0 gives |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|. So DΦ(w) is injective and T_w := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) has dimension n. Φ is injective on Ω; for y ∈ N let w_y ∈ Ω be the unique point with Φ(w_y) = y, and T_y := T_{w_y}. (The Lean conclusion “∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → …” concerns exactly w = w_y.)
 (b) Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : N → Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz. N is σ-compact (Ω is a countable union of compact sets and Φ is continuous), hence Borel; M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable.
 (c) N is locally Hⁿ-finite: if K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact, Ψ(N ∩ K) has diameter ≤ diam(K)/c, so lies in a closed ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ; Φ is Lipschitz on B̄ (C¹ on a compact convex set), say with constant Λ, and Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.
 (d) (Change of variables under blow-ups.) η_{y,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹, so for every set S and every g ≥ 0 or Hⁿ⌞S-integrable g: ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n} ∫_S g∘η_{y,λ} dHⁿ (translation invariance and μHE[n](λS) = λⁿ μHE[n](S), Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`).
 (e) (C¹ blow-up of N; Simon: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η(N_j)} f = ∫_{T N_j} f”.) For every y ∈ N and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q): lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ. Proof: let spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), w := w_y. By (d) and the injective area formula for Φ on Ω (Φ injective, Lipschitz on bounded subsets of Ω; Simon Ch. 2 (3.2)/(3.5), SimonGMT `injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn` and its weighted fibre-sum form) the integral equals λ^{−n} ∫_Ω φ((Φ(v) − y)/λ) JΦ(v) dv, JΦ(v) := √det(DΦ(v)*DΦ(v)), and the substitution v = w + λs turns it into I_λ := ∫ 1_{(Ω−w)/λ}(s) φ((Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ) JΦ(w+λs) ds. If the integrand is nonzero then w, w + λs ∈ Ω and |Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w)| < λR, so c|λs| < λR, i.e. |s| < R/c. For λ ≤ 1 the integrand is bounded by sup|φ| · max_{|z−w| ≤ R/c} JΦ(z) and vanishes for |s| ≥ R/c; for fixed s, as λ ↓ 0: w + λs ∈ Ω eventually (Ω open), (Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ → DΦ(w)s and JΦ(w+λs) → JΦ(w). By dominated convergence I_λ → ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(DΦ(w)s) JΦ(w) ds = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ, the last equality being the linear area formula for the injective linear map DΦ(w) (Simon Ch. 2 (3.1); Mathlib `LinearMap.hausdorffMeasure_image`/normDet). Note that for nonnegative φ ≥ 1_{B_R(0)} this also shows sup_{0<λ≤1} λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) < ∞.
 (f) (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`.) If μ is a Borel regular measure on ℝ^Q and A is μ-measurable with μ(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^Q ∖ A, lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} μ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) = 0. (Finite Borel measures on ℝ^Q, and Hⁿ restricted to sets of finite measure, are Borel regular.)

1. (Compact pieces with continuous weight — Remark 1.8(1).) Let V_1 ⊆ V_2 ⊆ ⋯ be open sets with compact closures closure V_i ⊆ V_{i+1} ⊆ V and ⋃_i V_i = V. Fix i. ν_i(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M ∩ V_i} θ dHⁿ defines a finite Borel measure (∫_{M ∩ closure V_i} θ < ∞), and θ is ν_i-measurable (θ is a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ closure V_i by `IntegrableOn`). Choose a Borel M_i′ ⊆ M ∩ V_i with Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ M_i′) = 0. For each j ≥ 1, Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure ν_i (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.Lusin`) gives a closed F with ν_i(ℝ^Q ∖ F) < 1/(2j) and θ|F continuous, and inner regularity gives a compact C_{i,j} ⊆ M_i′ ∩ F with ν_i((M_i′ ∩ F) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/(2j). Thus C_{i,j} ⊆ M ∩ V_i is compact, θ|C_{i,j} is continuous and ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/j. Hence ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0, and since θ > 0 on M, also Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0. As M = ⋃_i (M ∩ V_i), it suffices to prove: for each fixed C := C_{i,j}, the conclusion holds at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N. Note that θ ≥ m_C := min_C θ > 0 on C (continuous positive function on a compact set), so Hⁿ(C) ≤ m_C^{−1} ∫_C θ dHⁿ < ∞.

2. (Unweighted tangent plane of C on the chart — proof of 1.6 “⇒”.) Exceptional sets, by (f):
 (i) μ := Hⁿ⌞C (finite), A := C ∖ N: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 (ii) For each of the countably many rational balls B ⊆ ℝ^Q, μ := Hⁿ⌞(N ∩ B) (finite by (c)), A := (N ∩ B) ∖ C: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ B, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0; since B_ρ(y) ⊆ B for small ρ when y ∈ B, and the rational balls cover ℝ^Q: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy (i) and (ii). For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), using (d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ − ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N ∖ C)} φ + ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C ∖ N)} φ,
 and |∫_{η_{y,λ}(N∖C)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, |∫_{η_{y,λ}(C∖N)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, while the first term tends to ∫_{T_y} φ by (e). Hence lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ (the exceptional set does not depend on φ). Moreover λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) ≤ λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) + λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) stays bounded as λ ↓ 0 (by (e) and (i)).

3. (Exceptional set for the rest of M.) By (f) with μ := ν_i and A := (M ∩ V_i) ∖ C (ν_i(A) < ∞): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C, ρ^{−n} ∫_{((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0.

4. (Weighted blow-up — Remark 1.8(1).) Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy the conclusions of steps 2 and 3, let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), and let λ > 0 be so small that closure B_{λR}(y) ⊆ V_i (possible: y ∈ C ⊆ V_i open). Then z ↦ φ(z)θ(y + λz) is Hⁿ-integrable on η_{y,λ}(M): it vanishes unless y + λz ∈ M ∩ B_{λR}(y), and by (d) its absolute integral is ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{M ∩ closure B_{λR}(y)} θ < ∞. By (d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y+λz) dHⁿ(z) = λ^{−n} ∫_M φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) = I₁ + I₂ + I₃, where
 I₁ := θ(y) λ^{−n} ∫_C φ((x−y)/λ) dHⁿ(x) = θ(y) ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ → θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ (step 2);
 I₂ := λ^{−n} ∫_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ)(θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x), |I₂| ≤ sup|φ| · sup_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} |θ − θ(y)| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, because θ|C is continuous at y and the density ratio is bounded (step 2);
 I₃ := λ^{−n} ∫_{(M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x), and since (M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y) = ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y), |I₃| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{((M∩V_i)∖C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0 (step 3).
 Hence the weighted blow-up integrals converge to θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q); together with dim T_y = n (0(a)) this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T_y with T_y = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w_y).

5. (Conclusion.) The set of y ∈ M ∩ N where the conclusion fails is contained in ⋃_i ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) ∪ ⋃_{i,j} (the exceptional subsets of C_{i,j} ∩ N from steps 2–3), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Since M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable (0(b)), this is exactly the statement “∀ᵐ y ∂ Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(w))”. ∎
 (For n = 0 all steps hold verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, λ⁰ = 1, N is a single point or empty and T_y = {0}.)
proof_key_steps: Chart facts: DΦ(w) injective with |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|, Φ(Ω) σ-compact and locally Hⁿ-finite, inverse (1/c)-Lipschitz.
C¹ blow-up: via the injective area formula and dominated convergence, blow-ups of Φ(Ω) at y = Φ(w) converge to Hⁿ⌞DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ).
Remark 1.8(1): by Lusin, M ∩ V_i is covered up to null sets by compact C with θ|C continuous and Hⁿ(C) < ∞.
Proof of 1.6 ⇒: by the Upper Density Theorem, Hⁿ⌞(C∖N) and Hⁿ⌞(N∖C) have zero density at a.e. point of C ∩ N, so blow-ups of C converge to T_y with bounded density ratios.
Weighted blow-up of (M,θ) = θ(y)·blow-up of C + continuity error on C + θHⁿ⌞(M∖C) term of zero density, giving the weighted tangent space T_y.

subproblems.title: Change of variables through an injective Lipschitz–antilipschitz chart
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0, A ⊆ Φ(Ω) Hⁿ-null-measurable, and g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞A. Let D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩), DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w. Then D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, g∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D, and ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen Ω → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → A ⊆ Φ '' Ω → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → AEMeasurable g ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict A) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ AEMeasurable (fun w => g (Φ w)) ((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A)) ∧ ∫⁻ x in A, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫⁻ w in Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A, g (Φ w) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is step 4 of the parent proof (area formula for the injective Lipschitz chart Φ_j, transferring integrals over A_j to D_j, with the null-measurability of D_j and the a.e.-measurability of g∘Φ_j from step 1), for a single chart.

1. Φ is injective on Ω (if Φ(w) = Φ(w′) then c|w − w′| ≤ 0) and continuous on Ω (Lipschitz on Ω).
2. (Borel preimages.) For every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) is Borel: the map Φ̃ := Ω.piecewise Φ 0 (Φ on Ω, 0 off Ω) is Borel measurable (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, Φ continuous on the measurable set Ω, the constant continuous on Ωᶜ), and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) = Ω ∩ Φ̃⁻¹(B).
3. (First conclusion.) Choose a Borel B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(A ∖ B) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then D = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A ∖ B)); the first set is Borel by step 2 and the second is Lⁿ-null by the sibling lemma chart_preimage_null (with Z := A ∖ B). Hence D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
4. (Second conclusion.) Choose a measurable g′ with g = g′ Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. Since A is null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞A(E) = Hⁿ(E ∩ A) for every E (Measure.restrict_apply₀'), so Z′ := {x : g(x) ≠ g′(x)} ∩ A is Hⁿ-null, and by chart_preimage_null Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′)) = 0. For w ∈ D outside Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′) we have Φ(w) ∈ A and g(Φ(w)) = g′(Φ(w)). Since Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. w lies in D (D null-measurable, ae_restrict_mem₀) and outside the null set Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z′) (ae_restrict_of_ae), g∘Φ = g′∘Φ Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. Moreover Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞Ω (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable), hence for Lⁿ⌞D (D ⊆ Ω), so g′∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D (Measurable.comp_aemeasurable) and so is g∘Φ (AEMeasurable.congr).
5. (Area formula for Φ on D.) Φ is Lipschitz on Ω, hence locally Lipschitz on Ω (at each point use the neighbourhood Ω itself, self_mem_nhdsWithin). Apply the sibling lemma local_lipschitz_area with Q := P, the open set Ω, D ⊆ Ω (null-measurable by step 3), u := Φ and weight w ↦ g(Φ(w)) (a.e.-measurable by step 4): ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w) = ∫_{ℝ^P} N dHⁿ with N(y) := Σ_{w ∈ D, Φ(w) = y} g(Φ(w)).
6. (Fibres.) N = 1_A·g pointwise. If y ∈ A, then y = Φ(w₀) for some w₀ ∈ Ω (A ⊆ Φ(Ω)); w₀ ∈ D and, by injectivity of Φ on Ω, the fibre {w ∈ D : Φ(w) = y} is exactly {w₀}, so N(y) = g(Φ(w₀)) = g(y) (tsum_eq_single). If y ∉ A, no w ∈ D satisfies Φ(w) = y because Φ(w) ∈ A for w ∈ D; the fibre is empty and N(y) = 0.
7. (Third conclusion.) ∫ N dHⁿ = ∫ 1_A·g dHⁿ = ∫_A g dHⁿ (lintegral_indicator₀, A null-measurable). With step 5, ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_D g(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dLⁿ(w). ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ is injective and continuous on Ω; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Borel) is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise).
D = Borel part ∪ preimage of an Hⁿ-null set, null by chart_preimage_null: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
g∘Φ = g′∘Φ a.e. on D (g′ measurable) using chart_preimage_null on {g ≠ g′} ∩ A: a.e.-measurability.
local_lipschitz_area for u := Φ, weight g∘Φ on D ⊆ Ω.
By injectivity the fibre sum equals the indicator 1_A g; lintegral_indicator₀ gives ∫_A g dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Pulling Hⁿ-a.e. properties of M ∩ Φ(Ω) back to Lⁿ-a.e. parameters of an antilipschitz chart
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be (Borel) measurable, and let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be (Borel) measurable with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, for some c > 0. Let p be any property of points of ℝ^P that holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M ∩ Φ(Ω) (∀ᵐ x for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))). Then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable (Lⁿ = volume), and p(Φ(w)) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) (∀ᵐ w for Lⁿ⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (p : Eucl P → Prop), MeasurableSet Ω → Measurable Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ Φ '' Ω)), p x) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), p (Φ w)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure) on ℝ^P; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. For a measure μ and a set A, μ⌞A = μ.restrict A, and “q holds μ⌞A-a.e.” means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), q x. Write S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M).

This is steps 1–3 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule): Hⁿ-null exceptional sets in M ∩ Φ(Ω) pull back to Lⁿ-null sets of parameters, and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable, so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))-a.e. statements become Lⁿ⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))-a.e. statements.

0. (Null sets pull back.) Fix c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. The sibling lemma chart_preimage_null (Submission.lpf_raf_chart_preimage_null) applied to (P, n, Φ, Ω, c) gives:
(N) for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.

1. (S is Lⁿ-null-measurable.) Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, there is a measurable set B ⊆ M with B = M Hⁿ-a.e. (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq); in particular Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0 (ae_eq_set). Because B ⊆ M,
S = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B)):
if w ∈ S and Φ(w) ∈ B, then w lies in the first set; if w ∈ S and Φ(w) ∉ B, then Φ(w) ∈ M ∖ B and w lies in the second set; conversely both sets are contained in S because B ⊆ M and M ∖ B ⊆ M. The first set is measurable, since Ω and B are measurable sets and Φ is a measurable map. The second set has Lⁿ-measure 0 by (N) with Z := M ∖ B. The union of a measurable set and an Lⁿ-null set is Lⁿ-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet, NullMeasurableSet.of_null, NullMeasurableSet.union). Hence S is Lⁿ-null-measurable; this is the first conjunct.

2. (The exceptional set in ℝ^P is Hⁿ-null.) Let Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ¬p(x)} ∩ (M ∩ Φ(Ω)). The hypothesis ∀ᵐ x ∂(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))), p x says exactly (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)))({x : ¬p(x)}) = 0 (ae_iff). For every measure μ and all sets s, t one has μ(t ∩ s) ≤ (μ⌞s)(t), with no measurability assumption on s or t (Mathlib Measure.le_restrict_apply). With s := M ∩ Φ(Ω) and t := {x : ¬p(x)} this gives Hⁿ(Z) ≤ 0, so Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

3. (The exceptional set of parameters is Lⁿ-null.) By (N), Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0. Let w ∈ S with ¬p(Φ(w)). Then w ∈ Ω, Φ(w) ∈ M, Φ(w) ∈ Φ(Ω) because w ∈ Ω, and ¬p(Φ(w)); hence Φ(w) ∈ Z and w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z). Thus {w : ¬(w ∈ S → p(Φ(w)))} = {w : w ∈ S ∧ ¬p(Φ(w))} ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z), so this set is Lⁿ-null by monotonicity (measure_mono_null), i.e. ∀ᵐ w ∂Lⁿ, w ∈ S → p(Φ(w)) (ae_iff).

4. (Conclusion.) Since S is Lⁿ-null-measurable (step 1), for every property q one has (∀ᵐ w ∂(Lⁿ⌞S), q(w)) ⟺ (∀ᵐ w ∂Lⁿ, w ∈ S → q(w)) (Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'₀). Applying this with q(w) := p(Φ(w)) to step 3 gives ∀ᵐ w ∂(Lⁿ⌞S), p(Φ(w)), the second conjunct. ∎

(Remark: the null-measurability of S from step 1 is what makes step 4 valid; for a non-measurable S the measure Lⁿ⌞S need not be concentrated on S.)
proof_key_steps: chart_preimage_null: every Hⁿ-null Z ⊆ ℝ^P has Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.
Choose a measurable B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B)) is measurable ∪ Lⁿ-null, hence Lⁿ-null-measurable.
Z := {¬p} ∩ (M ∩ Φ(Ω)) satisfies Hⁿ(Z) ≤ (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)))({¬p}) = 0 (Measure.le_restrict_apply).
{w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) : ¬p(Φ w)} ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) is Lⁿ-null, and ae_restrict_iff'₀ (using null-measurability) turns this into the restricted a.e. statement.

subproblems.title: Moore–Penrose left inverse: continuous on injective maps, with projection bound
subproblems.statement: For all n, P there is a map Λ : L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ), continuous on the set of injective linear maps, such that for every injective A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P): Λ(A)∘A = id_{ℝⁿ} and |A(Λ(A)v)| ≤ |v| for every v ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n P : ℕ), ∃ Λ : (Eucl n →L[ℝ] Eucl P) → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl n), ContinuousOn Λ {A : Eucl n →L[ℝ] Eucl P | Function.Injective A} ∧ ∀ A : Eucl n →L[ℝ] Eucl P, Function.Injective A → (Λ A).comp A = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Eucl n) ∧ ∀ v : Eucl P, ‖A (Λ A v)‖ ≤ ‖v‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Lean `Eucl m`) with Euclidean norm |·| = ‖·‖; L(E, F) is the space of (continuous) linear maps with the operator norm; Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure (on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume); B_ρ(x) is the open ball. This is the linear-algebra input to Step 2 of the parent proof (the Moore–Penrose left inverse A⁺ = (A*A)⁻¹A* of an injective A, Step 2: A⁺A = id and AA⁺ = orthogonal projection onto range A). Fix n, P. For A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P) let A* ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ) be its adjoint (⟨A*y, s⟩ = ⟨y, As⟩; Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint). Let R := L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), a complete normed ring under composition, and let inv : R → R be the ring inverse (inv(T) = T⁻¹ if T is a unit of R, inv(T) = 0 otherwise; Mathlib Ring.inverse). Define
   Λ(A) := inv(A*A) ∘ A* ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ).

1. (A*A is a unit when A is injective.) Let A be injective. If A*As = 0 then |As|² = ⟨As, As⟩ = ⟨A*As, s⟩ = 0, so As = 0 and s = 0. Thus A*A is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, hence surjective (rank–nullity; Mathlib LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective), hence a linear bijection whose inverse is automatically continuous (finite dimension; LinearEquiv.ofBijective, LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv). So A*A is a unit of R, and inv(A*A)(A*A) = 1 = (A*A)inv(A*A) (Ring.inverse_mul_cancel, Ring.mul_inverse_cancel). (Mathlib also records ker(A*A) = ker A as adjoint_comp_self_injective_iff.)

2. (Left inverse.) For injective A: Λ(A)∘A = inv(A*A)∘(A*A) = id_{ℝⁿ}.

3. (Continuity on the injective maps.) Let A₀ be injective. The map A ↦ A* is continuous (it is a linear isometric equivalence), and composition (S, T) ↦ S∘T is continuous (bounded bilinear), so a(A) := A*A is continuous in A. By step 1, a(A₀) is a unit of the complete normed ring R, and the ring inverse is continuous at every unit (Mathlib NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt), so A ↦ inv(a(A)) is continuous at A₀. Composing again with the continuous A ↦ A* (continuity of composition), Λ(A) = inv(a(A))∘A* is continuous at A₀. Continuity at each point of the set I := {A : A injective} gives continuity of Λ on I.

4. (Projection bound.) Let A be injective, v ∈ ℝ^P, and p := AΛ(A)v. Then A*p = (A*A)inv(A*A)A*v = A*v by step 1, so A*(v − p) = 0. Hence for every s ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨v − p, As⟩ = ⟨A*(v − p), s⟩ = 0. Taking s := Λ(A)v gives ⟨v − p, p⟩ = 0, so by Pythagoras |v|² = |(v − p) + p|² = |v − p|² + |p|² ≥ |p|², i.e. |AΛ(A)v| = |p| ≤ |v|.

Steps 2–4 give the three required properties of Λ. ∎ (Degenerate cases are covered: for n = 0, R is the zero ring, every A is injective and Λ(A) = 0 works with the same proof; for n > P there is no injective A and only the existence of Λ is asserted.)
proof_key_steps: Define Λ(A) := Ring.inverse(A*A) ∘ A* (Moore–Penrose left inverse).
For injective A, A*A is injective (|As|² = ⟨A*As, s⟩), hence invertible in finite dimension.
Λ(A)A = (A*A)⁻¹(A*A) = id.
Adjoint, composition and ring inverse (continuous at units) are continuous, so Λ is continuous at every injective A.
A*(v − AΛ(A)v) = 0, so v − AΛ(A)v ⊥ AΛ(A)v and Pythagoras gives |AΛ(A)v| ≤ |v|.

subproblems.title: Antilipschitz on an open neighbourhood gives the derivative lower bound c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s|
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, c ∈ ℝ and w ∈ Ω. Assume Φ is differentiable at w and c|v − v′| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(v′)| for all v, v′ ∈ Ω. Then c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s| for every s ∈ ℝⁿ, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and |·| is the Euclidean norm. (No sign condition on c is needed.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (c : ℝ) (w : Eucl n), IsOpen Ω → w ∈ Ω → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → (∀ v ∈ Ω, ∀ v' ∈ Ω, c * ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖Φ v - Φ v'‖) → ∀ s : Eucl n, c * ‖s‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ Φ w s‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (lower bound for L = DΦ(w)), stated for an arbitrary real c and a map that is only differentiable at w.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with Euclidean norm ‖·‖; L := fderiv ℝ Φ w.

1. (Setup.) Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ. Since Φ is differentiable at w, Φ has Fréchet derivative L at w (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt).

2. (Derivative along the line.)
 - The curve ℓ(t) := w + t•s (t ∈ ℝ) has derivative s at t = 0. Lean: ((hasDerivAt_id 0).smul_const s).const_add w, after simp rewrites (1 : ℝ) • s to s.
 - ℓ(0) = w + 0•s = w, so by the chain rule γ(t) := Φ(w + t•s) has derivative L s at t = 0. Lean: HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hline h, with h : w = w + 0•s.

3. (Slope limit.) By HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_right, t⁻¹•(γ(0 + t) − γ(0)) → L s as t → 0 with t > 0, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Here γ(0 + t) = Φ(w + (0 + t)•s) and γ(0) = Φ(w + 0•s). The norm is continuous (Tendsto.norm), so ‖t⁻¹•(γ(0 + t) − γ(0))‖ → ‖L s‖ along 𝓝[>] 0.

4. (The line stays in Ω for small t.) The map t ↦ w + t•s is continuous and equals w at t = 0. Ω is open with w ∈ Ω, so Ω ∈ 𝓝 w (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Hence {t : w + t•s ∈ Ω} ∈ 𝓝 0 (ContinuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds), and it also belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (nhdsWithin_le_nhds).

5. (Inequality for small positive t.) By step 4 and self_mem_nhdsWithin, 𝓝[>]0-eventually every t satisfies t > 0 and w + t•s ∈ Ω. Fix such a t.
 - Apply the hypothesis to v := w + t•s ∈ Ω and v′ := w ∈ Ω. Since (w + t•s) − w = t•s (add_sub_cancel_left), this gives c‖t•s‖ ≤ ‖Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)‖.
 - Because t > 0, ‖t•s‖ = |t|·‖s‖ = t‖s‖ (norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg). So c·(t‖s‖) ≤ X, where X := ‖Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)‖.
 - Also ‖t⁻¹•(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w))‖ = t⁻¹·X, since t⁻¹ ≥ 0.
 - For t > 0, c‖s‖ ≤ t⁻¹·X ⟺ t·(c‖s‖) ≤ X (le_inv_mul_iff₀). And t·(c‖s‖) = c·(t‖s‖) ≤ X (linarith).
 - Hence, after simp rewrites 0 + t to t and 0•s to 0: c‖s‖ ≤ ‖t⁻¹•(γ(0 + t) − γ(0))‖ for 𝓝[>]0-eventually all t.

6. (Pass to the limit.) The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial. Steps 3 and 5 give an eventual lower bound for a convergent real sequence-like family, so the bound passes to the limit (ge_of_tendsto): c‖s‖ ≤ ‖L s‖. Since s was arbitrary, c‖s‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ Φ w s‖ for all s. ∎

Lean remark. The following proof was verified in the exact comparator scope as the declaration `theorem Submission.lpf_wtc_cat_fderiv_lower_bound : (<frozen statement>) := by` inside `namespace GMT.Ch06` of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
  intro Q n Φ Ω c w hΩ hw hdiff hanti s
  have hline : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) s 0 := by
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).smul_const s).const_add w
  have hγ : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => Φ (w + t • s)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w s) 0 := by
    have h0 : w + (0 : ℝ) • s = w := by simp
    exact hdiff.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hline h0.symm
  have hslope := hγ.tendsto_slope_zero_right
  have hnorm : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => ‖t⁻¹ • (Φ (w + (0 + t) • s) - Φ (w + (0 : ℝ) • s))‖)
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 ‖fderiv ℝ Φ w s‖) := hslope.norm
  have hcont : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => w + t • s) := continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)
  have hmem : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), w + t • s ∈ Ω := by
    apply hcont.continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds
    simpa using hΩ.mem_nhds hw
  have hev : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ‖s‖ ≤ ‖t⁻¹ • (Φ (w + (0 + t) • s) - Φ (w + (0 : ℝ) • s))‖ := by
    filter_upwards [nhdsWithin_le_nhds hmem, self_mem_nhdsWithin] with t ht htpos
    have htpos : (0 : ℝ) < t := htpos
    have h1 := hanti (w + t • s) ht w hw
    simp only [zero_add, zero_smul, add_zero]
    rw [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg htpos.le] at h1
    rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr htpos.le)]
    rw [le_inv_mul_iff₀ htpos]
    linarith [h1]
  exact ge_of_tendsto hnorm hev
proof_key_steps: Chain rule: γ(t) = Φ(w + t•s) has derivative DΦ(w)s at t = 0.
Slope limit: t⁻¹(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w)) → DΦ(w)s as t → 0+ (HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_right), hence norms converge.
Ω open: w + t•s ∈ Ω for 𝓝[>]0-eventually all t.
Antilipschitz with v = w + t•s, v′ = w and division by t > 0: c‖s‖ ≤ ‖t⁻¹(Φ(w + t•s) − Φ(w))‖ eventually.
Pass to the limit with ge_of_tendsto: c‖s‖ ≤ ‖DΦ(w)s‖.

subproblems.title: Integrals converge if they converge on every piece of a countable measurable partition, under integrable domination (Tannery)
subproblems.statement: Let X be a measurable space, ν a measure on X, V_j ⊆ X (j ∈ ℕ) measurable and pairwise disjoint with ν(X ∖ ⋃_j V_j) = 0, b : X → ℝ ν-integrable, F_k : X → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) ν-integrable with |F_k(x)| ≤ b(x) for ν-a.e. x (for every k), and F_∞ : X → ℝ ν-integrable. If ∫_{V_j} F_k dν → ∫_{V_j} F_∞ dν as k → ∞ for every j, then ∫_X F_k dν → ∫_X F_∞ dν as k → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (V : ℕ → Set X) (b : X → ℝ) (F : ℕ → X → ℝ) (Flim : X → ℝ), (∀ j, MeasurableSet (V j)) → Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint V) → ν (⋃ j, V j)ᶜ = 0 → Integrable b ν → (∀ k, Integrable (F k) ν) → (∀ k, ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, ‖F k x‖ ≤ b x) → Integrable Flim ν → (∀ j, Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in V j, F k x ∂ν) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in V j, Flim x ∂ν))) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, F k x ∂ν) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, Flim x ∂ν))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (countable additivity of the integral over the disjoint chart pieces, then dominated convergence for series), stated for an abstract measure. Notation: Fl := F_∞; all integrals are Bochner integrals and ∫_V H dν := ∫ H d(ν⌞V).
1. (ν lives on ⋃_j V_j.) The set (⋃_j V_j)ᶜ is ν-null, i.e. ν-a.e. x lies in ⋃_j V_j. Hence ν⌞(⋃_j V_j) = ν (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem`, after rewriting with `ae_iff`).
2. (Countable additivity.) Let H : X → ℝ be ν-integrable. Then H is integrable on ⋃_j V_j, and because the V_j are measurable and pairwise disjoint, the series Σ_j ∫_{V_j} H dν converges with sum ∫_{⋃_j V_j} H dν (Mathlib `hasSum_integral_iUnion`). By step 1 this sum is ∫_X H dν. So HasSum (j ↦ ∫_{V_j} H dν) (∫_X H dν).
3. (Summable majorant.) Step 2 for H = b shows that B_j := ∫_{V_j} b dν is summable. For all k, j: |∫_{V_j} F_k dν| ≤ ∫_{V_j} |F_k| dν ≤ ∫_{V_j} b dν = B_j. The first inequality is `norm_integral_le_integral_norm`. The second is monotonicity of the integral (`integral_mono_ae`): |F_k| and b are integrable on V_j, and |F_k| ≤ b holds ν-a.e., hence ν⌞V_j-a.e. (`ae_restrict_of_ae`).
4. (Tannery's theorem.) Let a_k(j), a(j) ∈ ℝ with a_k(j) → a(j) as k → ∞ for every j, and |a_k(j)| ≤ B_j for all k, j, where Σ_j B_j < ∞. Then Σ_j a_k(j) → Σ_j a(j).
Proof. First, |a(j)| ≤ B_j by passing to the limit, so all series converge absolutely. Given ε > 0, choose a finite set T ⊆ ℕ with Σ_{j∉T} B_j < ε/3. Choose k₀ with |Σ_{j∈T}(a_k(j) − a(j))| < ε/3 for k ≥ k₀; this is a finite sum of convergent sequences. For k ≥ k₀,
|Σ_j a_k(j) − Σ_j a(j)| ≤ |Σ_{j∈T}(a_k(j) − a(j))| + Σ_{j∉T}|a_k(j)| + Σ_{j∉T}|a(j)| < ε.
This is Mathlib's `tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence` (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Tannery.lean). That file is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch06.Submission, so inline this ε/3 argument as a local `have` for f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ along `atTop`; Mathlib's proof compiles verbatim with the existing imports. Adding `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Tannery` to Submission.lean is an alternative.
5. (Conclusion.) Put a_k(j) := ∫_{V_j} F_k dν and a(j) := ∫_{V_j} Fl dν. The hypothesis gives a_k(j) → a(j) for every j, and step 3 gives |a_k(j)| ≤ B_j with Σ_j B_j < ∞. By step 4, Σ_j a_k(j) → Σ_j a(j). Step 2, applied to H = F_k and to H = Fl (both ν-integrable), gives Σ_j a_k(j) = ∫_X F_k dν for every k and Σ_j a(j) = ∫_X Fl dν (`HasSum.tsum_eq`). Hence ∫_X F_k dν → ∫_X Fl dν. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν is concentrated on ⋃_j V_j, so ∫_X H dν = Σ_j ∫_{V_j} H dν for every ν-integrable H (hasSum_integral_iUnion).
|∫_{V_j} F_k dν| ≤ B_j := ∫_{V_j} b dν, and Σ_j B_j = ∫_X b dν < ∞.
Tannery's theorem (dominated convergence for series, ε/3 argument) gives Σ_j ∫_{V_j} F_k dν → Σ_j ∫_{V_j} F_∞ dν.
Both series equal the full integrals ∫_X F_k dν and ∫_X F_∞ dν.

subproblems.title: Area formula on a bi-Lipschitz chart for Bochner integrals: ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_{Ω∩Φ⁻¹(A)} JΦ·F∘Φ dLⁿ
subproblems.statement: Let E be a real Banach space, P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0, i.e. κ|w − w'| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w')| for w, w' ∈ Ω. Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be Hⁿ-null-measurable and F : ℝ^P → E Hⁿ⌞A-integrable, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. Put D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}, with DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, w ↦ JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) is Lⁿ-integrable on D, and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dLⁿ(w).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (F : Eucl P → E), IsOpen Ω → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ κ : ℝ, 0 < κ ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, κ * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → A ⊆ Φ '' Ω → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → IntegrableOn F A (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ IntegrableOn (fun w => Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det • F (Φ w)) (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ ∫ x in A, F x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫ w in Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A, Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det • F (Φ w) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (the area formula on the chart, extended from nonnegative to signed integrands). Here F is any Banach-valued integrable function, which covers the real integrands of steps 8–9 and the vector field Y of step 8. The parent splits a real F into positive and negative parts; for Banach-valued F the same step is done once for the measures (step 4 below). Notation as in the statement; JΦ ≥ 0 because it is a square root.
1. (The nonnegative formula.) Apply the sibling chart_change_of_variables (lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables) to the same Φ, Ω, A. For every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] that is Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. measurable: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, g∘Φ is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. measurable, and ∫⁻_A g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_D g(Φ(w))·ofReal(JΦ(w)) dw. With g = 0 this already gives the first conclusion: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
2. (JΦ is Borel.) w ↦ DΦ(w) is Borel measurable for every map Φ (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). The map Λ ↦ √det(⟨Λe_i, Λe_j⟩)_{i,j} is continuous on the space of linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^P: the entries are continuous, det is a polynomial and √ is continuous (`fun_prop` proves it). So JΦ is Borel, and so is w ↦ JΦ(w).toNNReal.
3. (A measure on the parameter side.) Let ρ := Lⁿ⌞D with density ofReal∘JΦ (Mathlib `withDensity` with density w ↦ ↑(JΦ(w).toNNReal), which is ofReal(JΦ(w)) by definition). Φ is continuous on Ω (it is Lipschitz there) and Ω is open, so Φ is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. measurable (`ContinuousOn.aemeasurable`). Since D ⊆ Ω (`Measure.restrict_mono`), Φ is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. measurable. Since ρ ≪ Lⁿ⌞D (`withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`), Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable.
4. (Φ pushes ρ forward to Hⁿ⌞A.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then:
(Φ_#ρ)(S) = ρ(Φ⁻¹(S)) (`Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable`)
= ∫⁻_{Φ⁻¹(S)} ofReal(JΦ) d(Lⁿ⌞D) (`withDensity_apply'`; Lⁿ⌞D is s-finite)
= ∫⁻_D 1_S(Φ(w))·ofReal(JΦ(w)) dw (`lintegral_indicator₀`; Φ⁻¹(S) is Lⁿ⌞D-null-measurable by step 3, and 1_{Φ⁻¹(S)}·ofReal(JΦ) = (1_S∘Φ)·ofReal(JΦ) pointwise)
= ∫⁻_A 1_S dHⁿ (step 1 with the Borel function g = 1_S)
= Hⁿ(S ∩ A) = (Hⁿ⌞A)(S).
Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal, so Φ_#ρ = Hⁿ⌞A.
5. (Transfer of integrability and integral.) F is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable, i.e. Φ_#ρ-integrable. Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable and F is Φ_#ρ-a.e. strongly measurable. Hence F∘Φ is ρ-integrable (`integrable_map_measure`), and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫ F d(Φ_#ρ) = ∫ F(Φ(w)) dρ(w) (`integral_map`).
6. (Removing the density.) Let f := JΦ.toNNReal : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞), which is Borel. For any G : ℝⁿ → E: G is ρ-integrable iff w ↦ f(w)·G(w) is Lⁿ⌞D-integrable (`integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul`), and ∫ G dρ = ∫_D f(w)·G(w) dw (`integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul`). Because JΦ ≥ 0, f(w) = JΦ(w) as real numbers (`Real.coe_toNNReal`), so f(w)·G(w) = JΦ(w)·G(w) (`NNReal.smul_def`). Take G := F∘Φ. With step 5, w ↦ JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) is Lⁿ-integrable on D and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dw. ∎
proof_key_steps: chart_change_of_variables: D is null-measurable, and ∫⁻_A g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_D (g∘Φ)·JΦ dLⁿ for every measurable g ≥ 0.
JΦ is Borel (measurable fderiv composed with the continuous Gram-determinant map) and nonnegative.
With ρ := JΦ·Lⁿ⌞D, Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable and Φ_#ρ = Hⁿ⌞A (test on Borel sets with g = 1_S).
integral_map and integrable_map_measure transfer F to F∘Φ under ρ.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul and integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul turn ρ back into JΦ·Lⁿ⌞D.

subproblems.title: An integrable tangent field on a chart piece lifts to an integrable coefficient field c with DΦ·c = JΦ·(Y∘Φ)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0. Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be Hⁿ-null-measurable and Y : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Hⁿ⌞A-integrable, such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x, Y(x) ∈ range DΦ(w). Put D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}. Then there is c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, Lⁿ-integrable on Ω, with c(w) = 0 for every w ∉ D and DΦ(w)c(w) = JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)) for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof, the coefficient field c = 1_{E'}·JΦ·a with a = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ(Y∘Φ). Here the explicit left inverse (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ is replaced by the continuous left inverse Λ of the sibling continuous_left_inverse, which has exactly the properties used there. Notation as in the statement; A_w := DΦ(w).
1. (Left inverse.) The sibling continuous_left_inverse (lpf_tde_continuous_left_inverse) gives Λ : L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ), continuous on the set of injective linear maps, such that every injective B satisfies Λ(B)∘B = id and |B(Λ(B)v)| ≤ |v| for all v ∈ ℝ^P.
2. (Chart derivative bounds.) Φ is C¹, so it is differentiable everywhere and w ↦ A_w is continuous (`ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`). For w ∈ Ω, the sibling fderiv_lower_bound (lpf_wtc_cat_fderiv_lower_bound) gives κ|s| ≤ |A_w s| for all s ∈ ℝⁿ. Consequences: A_w is injective for w ∈ Ω, since A_w s = A_w s' gives κ|s − s'| ≤ 0, so s = s'. And for v ∈ ℝ^P, κ|Λ(A_w)v| ≤ |A_w Λ(A_w)v| ≤ |v|, i.e. |Λ(A_w)v| ≤ κ⁻¹|v|.
3. (Integrability of Z.) Apply the sibling chart_integral_eq with E := ℝ^P and F := Y (Y is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable). It gives: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and Z(w) := JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)) is Lⁿ-integrable on D.
4. (Definition.) Put f(w) := Λ(A_w)(Z(w)) and c := 1_D·f, so c = f on D and c = 0 off D. In particular c(w) = 0 for every w ∉ D.
5. (c is integrable on Ω.) Measurability: w ↦ Λ(A_w) is continuous on Ω. It is the composition of the continuous map w ↦ A_w, which sends Ω into the injective maps by step 2, with Λ, which is continuous there. So it is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable (Ω is open; `ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable`), hence Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. strongly measurable. Z is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. strongly measurable by step 3, and evaluation (B, v) ↦ Bv is continuous bilinear, so f is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. strongly measurable (`ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂` with the identity of L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ)).
Integrability: for every w ∈ D ⊆ Ω, |f(w)| ≤ κ⁻¹|Z(w)| by step 2, and κ⁻¹|Z| is integrable on D, so f is integrable on D (`Integrable.mono'`). D is null-measurable, so the extension by zero c = 1_D·f is Lⁿ-integrable on ℝⁿ (`IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator₀`), in particular on Ω.
6. (Pulling back the tangency.) Apply the sibling ae_pullback (lpf_ccr_ae_pullback) with M := A and p(x) := 'for every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x, Y(x) ∈ range A_w'. Its hypotheses hold: Ω is open, hence measurable; Φ is continuous, hence measurable; Φ is κ-antilipschitz on Ω; A is Hⁿ-null-measurable; and p holds Hⁿ-a.e. on A ∩ Φ(Ω) because it holds Hⁿ-a.e. on A ⊇ A ∩ Φ(Ω) (`ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset`). Hence p(Φ(w)) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D.
7. (The identity.) Let w ∈ D satisfy p(Φ(w)); by step 6 and `ae_restrict_mem₀`, Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D does. Apply p(Φ(w)) to the point w itself (w ∈ Ω, Φ(w) = Φ(w)): there is s ∈ ℝⁿ with A_w s = Y(Φ(w)). Then Z(w) = JΦ(w)·A_w s = A_w(JΦ(w)s). By step 1 (A_w is injective), c(w) = f(w) = Λ(A_w)A_w(JΦ(w)s) = JΦ(w)s. Therefore A_w c(w) = JΦ(w)·A_w s = JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Λ from continuous_left_inverse plays the role of (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ; with fderiv_lower_bound, DΦ(w) is injective and |Λ(DΦ(w))v| ≤ κ⁻¹|v| on Ω.
chart_integral_eq with F = Y: D is null-measurable and Z = JΦ·(Y∘Φ) is integrable on D.
c := 1_D·Λ(DΦ)(Z) is a.e. strongly measurable (Λ∘DΦ is continuous on Ω) and |c| ≤ κ⁻¹|Z|, so c is integrable on Ω and vanishes off D.
ae_pullback moves the tangency Y∘Φ ∈ range DΦ to a.e. w ∈ D, where Λ(DΦ)∘DΦ = id gives DΦ(w)c(w) = JΦ(w)Y(Φ(w)).

subproblems.title: Chain rule on a C¹ chart for a Lipschitz function with a tangential gradient: D(h∘Φ)(w) = ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)·⟩ a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0. Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Hⁿ-null-measurable, h : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A, every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x and every u ∈ range DΦ(w), the function s ↦ h(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), h∘Φ is Fréchet differentiable at w with derivative s ↦ ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)s⟩, i.e. the continuous linear map (innerSL ℝ (G(Φ(w)))) ∘ DΦ(w). Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ and DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7(c),(d) and 9(b) of the parent proof: Rademacher on the chart, the directional-derivative fact (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10), and uniqueness of derivatives. Notation: D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), A_w := DΦ(w), and K is a Lipschitz constant of Φ on Ω.
1. (Pulling back the hypothesis.) Let p(x) be the property: 'for every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x and every u ∈ range A_w, s ↦ h(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at 0'. Apply the sibling ae_pullback (lpf_ccr_ae_pullback) with M := A. Its hypotheses hold: Ω is open, hence measurable; Φ is continuous (C¹), hence measurable; Φ is κ-antilipschitz on Ω; A is Hⁿ-null-measurable; and p holds Hⁿ-a.e. on A ∩ Φ(Ω) because it holds Hⁿ-a.e. on A ⊇ A ∩ Φ(Ω) (`ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset`). The conclusion: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and p(Φ(w)) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D.
2. (Rademacher.) h∘Φ is (L·K)-Lipschitz on Ω (`LipschitzWith.comp_lipschitzOnWith`). By Rademacher's theorem for maps Lipschitz on a set (Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem`), for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ with w ∈ Ω, h∘Φ is differentiable within Ω at w. Since Ω is open (Ω ∈ 𝓝 w), h∘Φ is then differentiable at w (`DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt`). Restricting to D ⊆ Ω (`ae_restrict_of_ae`): h∘Φ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D.
3. Fix w ∈ D at which steps 1 and 2 hold; Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D qualifies, using also `ae_restrict_mem₀` to get w ∈ D. Let B := D(h∘Φ)(w) and x := Φ(w). Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ, and put u := A_w s ∈ range A_w and φ₂(t) := h(x + t·u).
(a) Applying p(x) to the point w itself, φ₂ has derivative ⟨G(x), A_w s⟩ at t = 0.
(b) φ₂ also has derivative Bs at t = 0. The line t ↦ w + ts has derivative s. By the chain rule (`HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt`), φ₁(t) := (h∘Φ)(w + ts) has derivative Bs at 0, and t ↦ Φ(w + ts) has derivative A_w s at 0, i.e. Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − tA_w s = o(t). Since h is L-Lipschitz,
|φ₂(t) − φ₁(t)| = |h(x + tA_w s) − h(Φ(w + ts))| ≤ L·|Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − tA_w s| = o(t).
As φ₂(0) = φ₁(0) = h(x),
φ₂(t) − φ₂(0) − t·Bs = [φ₁(t) − φ₁(0) − t·Bs] + [φ₂(t) − φ₁(t)] = o(t).
In Lean: `hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO`, then `IsBigO.of_bound` with constant L, `IsBigO.trans_isLittleO`, `IsLittleO.add` and `IsLittleO.congr_left`.
(c) By uniqueness of derivatives (`HasDerivAt.unique`), Bs = ⟨G(x), A_w s⟩.
4. Since s was arbitrary, B = (innerSL ℝ (G(x))) ∘ A_w as continuous linear maps, and h∘Φ has Fréchet derivative B at w (`DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt`). This holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D. ∎
proof_key_steps: ae_pullback moves the tangential-derivative hypothesis from Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A to Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A).
Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem) for h∘Φ, which is Lipschitz on the open set Ω.
Directional derivative: t ↦ h(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) has derivative D(h∘Φ)(w)s, since it differs from (h∘Φ)(w + ts) by at most L·o(t).
Uniqueness of derivatives gives D(h∘Φ)(w)s = ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)s⟩ for every s.

subproblems.title: Tangential integrals over a chart piece as parameter integrals against one integrable field: ∫_A Df(Y) = ∫_Ω D(f∘Φ)(c) and ∫_A ⟨G, Y⟩ = ∫_Ω D(h∘Φ)(c)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0. Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be Hⁿ-null-measurable, h : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |G| ≤ L everywhere, and Y : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Hⁿ⌞A-integrable. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x: Y(x) ∈ range DΦ(w), and for every u ∈ range DΦ(w), s ↦ h(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0. Then there is c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, Lⁿ-integrable on Ω, such that:
(i) ∫_A Df(x)(Y(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_Ω D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw for every differentiable f : ℝ^P → ℝ that is K-Lipschitz for some K ≥ 0;
(ii) ∫_A ⟨G(x), Y(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) = ∫_Ω D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw.
Here D = fderiv ℝ, which is 0 where the map is not differentiable; DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof, items (9a) and (9b): rewrite ∫_{M_j} F_k and ∫_{M_j} F_∞ as parameter integrals against the coefficient field. Steps 5, 7 and 8 of the parent are supplied by the three siblings. Notation: D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), A_w := DΦ(w), JΦ(w) := √det(⟨A_w e_i, A_w e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}. Φ is C¹, hence differentiable everywhere.
1. (Coefficient field.) Apply the sibling coefficient_field with the first half of the a.e. hypothesis (Y(x) ∈ range A_w). It gives c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, Lⁿ-integrable on Ω, with c(w) = 0 for w ∉ D and A_w c(w) = JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)) for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D. This c is the field in the conclusion.
2. (Differential of h∘Φ.) Apply the sibling chart_has_fderiv_at with the second half of the a.e. hypothesis. It gives: for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D, h∘Φ has Fréchet derivative v ↦ ⟨G(Φ(w)), A_w v⟩ at w. In particular D(h∘Φ)(w)v = ⟨G(Φ(w)), A_w v⟩ (`HasFDerivAt.fderiv`).
3. (Integrals over Ω reduce to D.) For any u : ℝⁿ → ℝ and w ∈ Ω ∖ D we have c(w) = 0, so Du(w)(c(w)) = 0. Since Ω is measurable and D ⊆ Ω, ∫_Ω Du(w)(c(w)) dw = ∫_D Du(w)(c(w)) dw (`setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`; no integrability is needed).
4. (Identity (i).) Let f be differentiable and K-Lipschitz, and put F(x) := Df(x)(Y(x)). F is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable:
- x ↦ Df(x) is Borel (`measurable_fderiv`), Y is Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. strongly measurable, and evaluation is continuous bilinear, so F is a.e. strongly measurable;
- |F(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖·|Y(x)| ≤ K|Y(x)| (`norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz`), and K|Y| is integrable on A.
The sibling chart_integral_eq with E := ℝ gives ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dw. For Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D (step 1), the chain rule (`fderiv_comp`; f is differentiable at Φ(w) and Φ at w) gives
D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = Df(Φ(w))(A_w c(w)) = Df(Φ(w))(JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w))) = JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)).
Hence ∫_D D(f∘Φ)(c) dLⁿ = ∫_D JΦ·(F∘Φ) dLⁿ (`integral_congr_ae`). With step 3, ∫_Ω D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw = ∫_A F dHⁿ.
5. (Identity (ii).) Put F(x) := ⟨G(x), Y(x)⟩. F is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable: G is Borel, Y is a.e. strongly measurable and the inner product is continuous (`continuous_inner.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂`); and |F| ≤ |G|·|Y| ≤ L|Y|. chart_integral_eq gives ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dw. For Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D (steps 1 and 2),
D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = ⟨G(Φ(w)), A_w c(w)⟩ = ⟨G(Φ(w)), JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w))⟩ = JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)).
With step 3, ∫_Ω D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw = ∫_D JΦ·(F∘Φ) dLⁿ = ∫_A ⟨G, Y⟩ dHⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: coefficient_field gives c integrable on Ω, c = 0 off D = Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), and DΦ(w)c(w) = JΦ(w)Y(Φ(w)) a.e. on D.
chart_has_fderiv_at gives D(h∘Φ)(w) = ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)·⟩ a.e. on D.
∫_Ω Du(c) = ∫_D Du(c) because c = 0 on Ω ∖ D.
Chain rule: a.e. on D, D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = JΦ(w)·Df(Φ(w))(Y(Φ(w))) and D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = JΦ(w)·⟨G, Y⟩(Φ(w)).
chart_integral_eq (E = ℝ) turns ∫_D JΦ·(F∘Φ) back into ∫_A F dHⁿ for F = Df(Y) and F = ⟨G, Y⟩; both are dominated by a constant times |Y|.
